title: a test run from a linked worktree never casts a live ticket
intention: A red measured in a builder's linked worktree is named as not ticketed and never becomes a live ticket; only the house tree's reds are cast.
why: Outline 9.4.2.3.7.5 wants every red ticketed, but a red-first run in a worktree is the build working, not a red lost. Read 2026-11-14 on akienyoga9i, while building 207c4074b3d5's FIXME 1 (branch fixme-207c4074b3d5, 80246bd57): cairn/tools/base/ticket_file.py:15 derives the store as <checkout>/../CairnCommons/tickets. On Windows every builder's worktree (C:/automation/local/cairn-<id>) is a sibling of the house commons, so that store resolves to the LIVE C:/automation/local/CairnCommons/tickets, in a git tree. red_tickets._rel keys a worktree's proof as inside its repo, and run_proof tickets every red. So a red-first `bin/cairn test` in a Windows worktree would cast a live ticket for a build in flight, and commit it into the house commons. This was read, not run: running it would cast the live ticket. On the Dell, /tmp worktrees have no sibling commons and hit StoreUnreachable instead (FIXME 1).
traces_to: Law 7 (the red stays in its record, and the not-ticketed is named); ticket 207c4074b3d5 (D7, FIXME 1)
how: D1: A LINKED WORKTREE NEVER CASTS. ticket_what_is_new asks git whether the repo it keys against is a linked worktree (`git rev-parse --git-dir` differs from `--git-common-dir`). If it is, the call casts nothing, commits nothing, and raises StoreUnreachable naming the worktree, so run_proof's FIXME 1 path prints '<proof> is red and was NOT ticketed: ...' and the run goes on. A proof's scratch repo, set through ROOTS['repo'] and made with git init, is a main tree and still casts, so 207c's teeth keep their world. Builds on 207c4074b3d5's FIXME 1 (StoreUnreachable). D2: PROOF, red-first. cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_worktree_run_casts_no_live_ticket.py: a scratch main repo, a linked worktree added from it, and a scratch commons in git standing where the worktree's sibling store resolves. One tooth per clause.

clauses.claim: a red run_proof over a proof in a linked worktree whose sibling ticket store is in a git tree casts no ticket and commits nothing to that commons
the same run returns its red record and names on stderr that the red was not ticketed because the checkout is a linked worktree
a red run over the same proof in the main tree still casts its ticket, so the guard is the worktree and not the red
